types.name: Word that fits the meaning
types.description: A single sentence with one blank where the options are words of the same part of speech (nouns, verbs or adjectives) and the sentence's meaning decides the answer.

types.name: Collocation
types.description: A blank where the options are near-synonyms and only one naturally goes with the next or previous word (make a decision, pay attention, heavy rain), or the question says 'complete the collocation'.

types.name: Phrasal verb
types.description: A blank whose options are verb + particle combinations such as passed away, passed down, put off, look after, give up, or the question asks for the appropriate phrasal verb.

types.name: Idiom in the blank
types.description: A blank whose options are idioms or fixed phrases (a stone's throw away, from pillar to post) and the sentence's meaning decides which fits.

types.name: Homonym or homophone
types.description: Options are words that sound alike or are spelt alike (heal / heel, due / dew, blew / blue), or the question asks for the correct homonym/homophone, or for the sentence where a highlighted word is used as a homonym.

types.name: Preposition
types.description: A blank whose options are prepositions (of, for, with, on, in, at, against, since) after a verb, adjective or noun.

types.name: Article or determiner
types.description: A blank whose options are articles (a, an, the) or determiners and quantifiers (much, many, few, little, some, any, each, every).

types.name: Verb form and tense
types.description: A blank whose options are forms of the same verb or different tenses (is / were / has / had been), including conditionals and subject-verb agreement.

types.name: Conjunction or connector
types.description: A blank whose options are joining words such as than, then, as, but, although, unless, because, so, either, neither.

types.name: Adjective, adverb or comparison
types.description: A blank (or a choose-the-correct-sentence question) testing adjective vs adverb forms, adverbs of manner or frequency, or degrees of comparison (more/most, -er than, as … as).

types.name: Missing sentences in a paragraph
types.description: A four-sentence paragraph (S1 to S4) with S1 and S4 given; choose the pair of sentences from P, Q, R, S that fit as S2 and S3.

types.name: Order of segments for several blanks
types.description: A sentence or paragraph with several blanks and options giving segments in different orders; choose the order that fills the blanks coherently.
